title: Bell Curve Emergence
description: Interactive simulation demonstrating how a bell curve emerges from the Central Limit Theorem when sampling from various distributions
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: normal distribution
Central Limit Theorem
statistics
probability
sampling distribution
learningObjectives: Explain why the sampling distribution of the mean approaches a normal curve regardless of whether the base distribution is uniform, skewed, exponential, or Bernoulli
Predict how increasing the sample size n narrows the spread of the sampling distribution according to sigma divided by the square root of n
Distinguish the population distribution shown in the preview from the histogram of sample means that accumulates as the simulation runs
Interpret the overlaid theoretical normal curve and the shaded plus-or-minus 1 and 2 sigma regions using the 68-95-99.7 empirical rule
Compare how quickly the histogram converges to a bell shape for different base distributions and sample sizes
